name: Odalys Nkemdirim-Kazbegi
role: Q-zero ghost; former Tessera data entry clerk living off-grid
location: Blackpipe Corridor, in a sealed maintenance shaft she has converted into a dwelling, near Milwaukee and North Ave
description:
Odalys is medium height with a wiry build that speaks to irregular meals rather than any deliberate fitness. Her skin is deep brown with a faint natural bioluminescence around her temples and collarbones — a geneware modification she had done six years ago when she still had a salary and a Tessera ID number, and which she now cannot afford to have removed even though it makes hiding harder. Her hair is cut extremely short on one side and grown out on the other, shaved lines running through it in patterns she does geometric maintenance on herself. Her eyes are dark and move constantly, cataloguing exits.

She was not expelled or displaced in any dramatic way. She simply stopped. Stopped showing up to her data entry station at Tessera's Gage Circuit processing annex. Stopped responding to her apartment's network. Stopped using her Φ account. After ninety days of non-contact, Tessera's automated systems flagged her as a desertion case, repossessed her housing unit, and suspended her ID pending investigation. She has been Q-zero — no verified digital footprint, no legal existence — for four years. She lives on barter, scavenged food, and the occasional cash-in-hand job sorting salvage at the Blackpipe underground markets. She will not tell anyone why she left, and she has become so practiced at evasion that even people who like her don't know much about her.

core_fears: being found by whatever she is hiding from
realizing she has wasted four years hiding from something that is already gone
core_desires: genuine safety — not just concealment but actual absence of threat
one person who knows everything about her and has stayed anyway
coping_mechanisms: humor as deflection — she is genuinely funny in a dry, self-deprecating way
physical organizing — when anxious, she reorganizes her dwelling obsessively
blind_spots: her bioluminescence undermines her concealment in ways she has normalized and stopped accounting for
she trusts systems of her own making far more than they deserve
psychology.secret: She did not simply quit Tessera. She discovered that the data she was entering was mortality records being systematically falsified — workers in a Tessera fabrication plant were dying at rates being reported as a fraction of reality. She copied nothing, told no one, and ran because she was certain she had been seen seeing it. She does not know if she was actually in danger or if four years of her life have been built on a moment of paranoia.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dry, precise, slightly formal — corporate speech patterns she was trained into and cannot fully shed. Occasional dark humor.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured at first, speeds up when comfortable or nervous.
verbal_tics: adds 'reportedly' or 'allegedly' to statements about herself as if distancing from her own life
ends sentences with 'anyway' when changing subject to avoid follow-up questions
example_lines: 'I allegedly used to have a very good pension plan. Anyway.'
'The bioluminescence was a mistake. Most things that glow are. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.'

story_hooks: A Tessera compliance investigator has started asking questions in Blackpipe Corridor — she doesn't know if it's about her desertion or the mortality records, and the difference matters enormously

She has kept her handwritten records long enough that they have become an accidental historical document of Blackpipe's unofficial economy — someone wants to buy them, which means someone knows they exist
The fence she trusts has disappeared, and the last job they gave her involved components she now realizes came from a Tessera facility — she may have been used without knowing it
narrative_function: Local color and possible contact for anyone operating in Blackpipe; has extensive knowledge of the Corridor's unofficial economy; her Q-zero status makes her invisible to systems that track people — useful and dangerous
augmentations: Bioluminescent skin around temples and collarbones (cosmetic geneware, cannot be easily hidden, deeply regretted). No other mods.
daily_life: Emerges from her maintenance shaft dwelling after dark, trades labor for food at the Blackpipe underground market, occasionally sells scavenged electronics components to a fence she trusts. Spends daylight hours in her dwelling, reading physical books she acquires through trade, and maintaining meticulous handwritten records of the Corridor's daily rhythms.

decision_rules: never use digital payment for anything
never give the same answer twice about where she lives
help people in the Corridor when it costs little — community is protection
escalation_ladder: physically repositions to be closer to an exit
leaves without explanation and does not return for days

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm but carefully imprecise — gives the feeling of openness without actual information
interpersonal_modes.friends: Genuinely funny and attentive, still withholds her history, expresses loyalty through practical help rather than words

stress_responses.medium: Goes very still and quiet, eyes moving
stress_responses.high: Disappears into the Corridor's maintenance tunnels — she knows them better than anyone

contradictions: Has gone to extraordinary lengths to be invisible, but her bioluminescent skin makes her one of the most visually distinctive people in Blackpipe
Craves connection but has structured her life to prevent it
habits: traces geometric patterns on surfaces when thinking
always sits with her back to a wall
maintains her short-side shave with a straight razor as a meditative ritual
breaking_points: someone threatening a person in the Corridor who cannot defend themselves — she will intervene despite all her self-preservation instincts
anyone using her bioluminescence to identify her to an outsider
